url = "/level-api/:step?" title = "Programmatic API" layout = "default" is_hidden = 0 [wizard] == wizard->define(function (WizardBuilder $builder) { $builder ->step('step-1', 'Step 1') ->fields([ ['name' => 'field1', 'label' => 'Field 1'], ]) ->rules(['field1' => 'required']) ->end() ->step('step-2', 'Step 2') ->fields([ ['name' => 'field2', 'label' => 'Field 2'], ]) ->rules(['field2' => 'required']) ->end() // A third step, so submitting step 2 does not finish the wizard // (a finished wizard clears the session). ->step('step-3', 'Step 3') ->fields([ ['name' => 'field3', 'label' => 'Field 3'], ]) ->rules(['field3' => 'required']) ->end(); }); } function onCartData() { $this->wizard->saveData(['cart_total' => post('cart_total', 0)], 'step-1'); return [ 'data' => $this->wizard->data(), 'stepCurrent' => $this->wizard->stepCurrent(), 'meta' => $this->wizard->meta(), ]; } /** * Reproduces the case the wizard-shop sample hit: a handler writes a key to an * EARLY step while a LATER step also stores that key, so the merged view * resolves the key to the later step and the write looks like it did nothing. * `stepData()` is the way to read back what you just wrote. */ function onShadowedWrite() { $this->wizard->saveData(['shared' => post('value', 'written')], post('step', 'step-1')); return [ 'merged' => $this->wizard->data(), 'step1' => $this->wizard->stepData('step-1'), 'step2' => $this->wizard->stepData('step-2'), ]; } /** * The v1 use case: the last step needs EVERY step's data to finish the order, * with nothing merged away. stepsData() returns the per-step map, so two steps * can hold the same key name without either hiding the other. */ function onAllSteps() { return ['steps' => $this->wizard->stepsData()]; } function onUnknownStepRead() { return ['data' => $this->wizard->stepData('nope')]; } function onBadSave() { $this->wizard->saveData(['x' => 1], 'nope'); } /** * The rename case: a key the wizard stored under an old name is removed. * Without a step code the key leaves every step. */ function onForget() { $this->wizard->forgetData((array) post('keys', ['stale']), post('step') ?: null); return [ 'merged' => $this->wizard->data(), 'steps' => $this->wizard->stepsData(), ]; } function onForgetUnknownStep() { $this->wizard->forgetData(['stale'], 'nope'); } /** * The handler guard: one call that both checks the step is reachable and * returns the data, so the check cannot be separated from the read. */ function onRequire() { $data = $this->wizard->requireData(post('step', 'step-2'), ['field2']); if ($this->wizard->needsRedirect($data)) { return $data; } return ['required' => $data]; } function onRequireUnknownStep() { return $this->wizard->requireData('nope'); } /** * The guard's own contract, exercised directly: the predicate has to answer * for BOTH shapes requireData() returns. Calling a method on the array is a * fatal error, so a predicate that only works on the response is unusable. */ function onGuardProbe() { return [ 'plain_array' => $this->wizard->needsRedirect(['totals' => 1]), 'empty_array' => $this->wizard->needsRedirect([]), 'response' => $this->wizard->needsRedirect(redirect('/level-api/step-1')), ]; } function onReset() { $this->wizard->flush(); } ?> == {% component 'wizard' %} {{ wizard.data.cart_total }} {{ wizard.stepNumber }} of {{ wizard.steps|length }}
